title: Oracle separation of BQP from efficient-prover interactive proofs
formal: Does there exist a classical Boolean oracle A and a language \(\mathrm{L}\subseteq \{0,1\}\)* such that \(\mathrm{L}\in \mathrm{BQP}^{A}\) but \(\mathrm{L}\notin \mathrm{IP}_{\mathrm{BQP}}^{A}\), where \(\mathrm{IP}_{\mathrm{BQP}}^{A}\) requires a polynomial-time quantum honest prover and classical interaction with a polynomial-time classical verifier?
why: Distinguishes the existence of a classical interactive proof from the ability of an efficient quantum device to carry out its honest strategy. It tests whether verification can match the computational resources of the device while retaining soundness against all cheating provers.
status_note: Source Problems 7–8 and the April 2026 paper checked; subsequent-work searches through 11 September 2026 located no resolution of the stated oracle question. The MIP containment changes the prover model and is recorded as preprint progress. This is a formulation and source review, not an exhaustive literature or proof audit.

progress.text: Aaronson states the oracle separation as Problem 8 and defines the distinction between IP and its efficient-quantum-honest-prover variant.

The preprint A Relativizing MIP for BQP states containment in classical MIP for every classical oracle and explicitly leaves the single-prover oracle separation open. The introduction also identifies efficient-honest-prover verification as an open issue. This review checked the statements and model, not the full proofs.

importance.reason: An oracle benchmark for the reach of efficient-prover interactive verification of quantum computation.

sentences: An efficient quantum computation can have a classical interactive proof whose honest prover is too expensive for the quantum device to execute.
This problem asks for an oracle relative to which some quantum polynomial-time language has no classical interactive proof with a quantum polynomial-time honest prover.
The verifier and honest prover access the same classical oracle, with quantum queries available only to the quantum computation.
Soundness must hold even against an unbounded dishonest prover, so computationally sound cryptographic arguments have a different guarantee.
A separation would expose an oracle obstruction to classical verification using only the computational power of an efficient quantum device.

upgraded_from.title: Oracle separation of BQP from efficient-prover interactive proofs

references.title: Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity

definitions: An oracle is an arbitrary fixed Boolean function \(A:\{0,1\}*\to \{0,1\}\); it need not be computable. All languages are subsets of \(\{0,1\}\)*, and n is the input length. A classical oracle call supplies one string z and returns \(A(z)\). Quantum access uses the unitary |\(z,b\rangle \mapsto |z,b\oplus A(z)\rangle\), extended linearly to superpositions of strings of a given length. Query registers and the work required to prepare them count toward the computation bound. No quantum-valued oracle, advice string or promise on inputs is supplied. \(\mathrm{BQP}^{A}\) consists of languages decided by one uniform quantum algorithm with polynomial total running time, oracle calls and qubits. On every yes input it accepts with probability at least \(2/3\), and on every no input with probability at most \(1/3\). One standard machine convention uses Hadamard \(H=(1/\sqrt{2})[[1,1],[1,- 1]], T=diag(1,e^{i\pi /4})\) and CNOT |\(a,b\rangle \mapsto |a,a\oplus b\rangle\) gates, zero-initialized auxiliary qubits, computational-basis measurements and polynomial-time classical control. Circuit descriptions are generated uniformly in polynomial time; there is no nonuniform advice. Probabilities are over measurements and any internal random bits. An \(\mathrm{IP}^{A}\) protocol has one classical probabilistic polynomial-time verifier and one prover, exchanging only classical bit strings. The verifier has private fair random bits and classical access to A. Its total computation, random bits, communication and number of rounds are bounded by a polynomial in n, with no predetermined universal degree. Completeness requires one honest prover strategy that makes the verifier accept with probability at least \(2/3\) on every yes input. Soundness requires acceptance probability at most \(1/3\) on every no input against every prover strategy, including computationally unbounded strategies. The prover knows the common input and oracle but not the verifier’s unrevealed private coins; its messages can depend on its conversation history. There is no trusted setup or shared entanglement. Prover efficiency is unrestricted in \(\mathrm{IP}^{A}\). Probabilities include verifier randomness and any randomness or measurements of the prover. \(\mathrm{IP}_{\mathrm{BQP}}^{A}\) is the subclass of \(\mathrm{BQP}^{A}\) whose languages admit such an \(\mathrm{IP}^{A}\) protocol with one uniform quantum polynomial-time oracle algorithm as the honest prover. Its total local work and oracle queries across all rounds are polynomial in n, under the same quantum access convention as \(\mathrm{BQP}^{A}\). Only the honest prover is restricted: soundness still quantifies over all computationally unbounded cheating strategies. Polynomial bounds and machines may depend on A and the language, but must work for all input lengths; they cannot depend on the particular input through advice.
answer_criterion: Prove the existence of one oracle A and \(\mathrm{BQP}^{A}\) language L for which no classical interactive proof has an honest quantum polynomial-time oracle prover. Alternatively, prove \(\mathrm{BQP}^{A}=\mathrm{IP}_{\mathrm{BQP}}^{A}\) for every classical Boolean oracle A. All negative instances must rule out arbitrary polynomial bounds on rounds and honest-prover work, and the positive alternative must retain soundness against unbounded cheating provers.

context_blocks.title: Can a classical verifier trust a quantum computation?
context_blocks.text: A proof of a quantum answer is useful for verification by a classical computer only if the honest quantum device can actually provide it. An interactive proof with an unrestricted prover does not guarantee this. This card asks whether some oracle world separates efficient quantum computation from verification with an efficient quantum honest prover.

context_blocks.title: The same function, different query access
context_blocks.text: The quantum computation may query a superposition, whereas the verifier queries one ordinary string at a time. The oracle function itself is identical for both. Some oracle languages are easy for both: for \(\mathrm{L}=\{x:A(x)=1\}\), the verifier simply queries x. The question requires a language whose quantum computation cannot be certified by the stated interaction.

context_blocks.title: Two distinct single-prover questions
context_blocks.text: For every oracle, \(\mathrm{IP}_{\mathrm{BQP}}^{A}\subseteq \mathrm{BQP}^{A}\) and \(\mathrm{IP}_{\mathrm{BQP}}^{A}\subseteq \mathrm{IP}^{A}\) by definition. An oracle separation of BQP from unrestricted-prover IP therefore also separates BQP from \(\mathrm{IP}_{\mathrm{BQP}}\). The efficient-honest-prover separation is a weaker demand: an unrestricted prover might still verify that language. The two cards record this implication without identifying the targets.

context_blocks.title: Unbounded cheating is part of the guarantee
context_blocks.text: The prover can lie in any computationally possible way, even with unlimited computation. Restricting only a dishonest prover to efficient strategies would instead describe a computationally sound argument. Cryptographic verification protocols with that guarantee do not establish the information-theoretic IP containment requested here.

context_blocks.title: What the 2026 multiple-prover result changes
context_blocks.text: Aaronson, Natarajan, Tal and Villányi state \(\mathrm{BQP}^{A}\subseteq MIP^{A}\) for every classical oracle. MIP permits several separated provers who cannot communicate during the protocol; the stated result uses classical provers without shared entanglement. The source still identifies the single-prover oracle question as open and does not supply a polynomial-time quantum honest prover for its MIP result.
